speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; let's begin by asking: when did these symptoms first start, and was there a fever or difficulty feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity at 33 weeks gestation. Given the onset within two hours of birth in a preterm infant, surfactant deficiency is the most likely cause. REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
